stem: National Emergency (Article 352) can be proclaimed on grounds of:

options.option_text: War, external aggression, or armed rebellion

explanation: Article 352 allows National Emergency due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion ('internal disturbance' was the original term — changed to 'armed rebellion' by the 44th Amendment, 1978).
subject: Polity

stem: The 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978) made which important change to National Emergency provisions?

options.option_text: Replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' and required Cabinet written advice
Extended the duration from 6 months to 1 year

explanation: The 44th Amendment (1978): (1) replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' to prevent misuse; (2) made it mandatory for the Cabinet (not just PM alone) to tender written advice to the President; (3) required approval by special majority in Parliament.
subject: Polity

stem: During a National Emergency, how many days does the Lok Sabha have to approve the proclamation?
explanation: A National Emergency must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within one month by a special majority (2/3 of members present and voting, which must also be a majority of total House membership). Post-44th Amendment.
subject: Polity

stem: President's Rule (Article 356) is imposed when:

options.option_text: The Governor reports that the State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution

explanation: Article 356 (President's Rule / State Emergency) is imposed on receipt of a report from the Governor OR if the President is otherwise satisfied that constitutional government in a State has broken down.
subject: Polity

stem: For how long can President's Rule (Article 356) be extended, with Parliamentary approval every 6 months, up to a maximum of:
explanation: President's Rule can initially last for 6 months; extended up to 1 year with Parliament's approval every 6 months. Beyond 1 year, extension up to 3 years is allowed only if a National Emergency is in force OR if the Election Commission certifies that elections in the State cannot be held.
subject: Polity

stem: Financial Emergency (Article 360) has been proclaimed in India:
explanation: Financial Emergency (Article 360) has never been proclaimed in India. National Emergency has been proclaimed three times (1962, 1971, 1975); President's Rule has been imposed many times in various states.
subject: Polity

stem: During Financial Emergency (Article 360), the President can direct states to:

options.option_text: Observe canons of financial propriety and reduce salaries of government servants including judges
Surrender their legislative powers to Parliament

explanation: During Financial Emergency, the President can direct: all money bills to be reserved for President's assent; states to reduce salaries of government servants; salaries/allowances of High Court and Supreme Court judges may be reduced.
subject: Polity

stem: The Supreme Court in Bommai v. Union of India (1994) held that imposition of President's Rule is subject to:
explanation: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) — landmark judgment: imposition of President's Rule is judicially reviewable; it cannot be used arbitrarily. The floor test in the Assembly is the proper method to test whether the government commands majority support.
subject: Polity

stem: How many times has National Emergency been proclaimed in India?
explanation: India has had three National Emergencies: (1) 1962 — China war; (2) 1971 — Indo-Pak war; (3) 1975 — 'internal disturbance' (the infamous Emergency under Indira Gandhi, revoked in 1977).
subject: Polity

stem: During a National Emergency, Fundamental Rights under Article 19 are automatically suspended for citizens of:

options.option_text: Only the state where the emergency was proclaimed
States at war — if external aggression or war

explanation: Article 358: During National Emergency on grounds of war/external aggression, Article 19 rights are automatically suspended. During emergency due to armed rebellion only, Article 19 suspension is not automatic — requires a separate order under Article 359.
subject: Polity

stem: Under Article 359, during a National Emergency, enforcement of which rights can be suspended by Presidential order?

options.option_text: All Fundamental Rights including Articles 20 and 21
All Fundamental Rights except Articles 20 and 21

explanation: Article 359 allows the President to suspend the right to move courts for enforcement of Fundamental Rights during Emergency — but Articles 20 (protection in conviction) and 21 (right to life and liberty) CANNOT be suspended. This protection was added by the 44th Amendment.
subject: Polity

stem: Which emergency provision in India is also called the 'constitutional breakdown' clause?
explanation: Article 356 (President's Rule) is often called the 'constitutional breakdown clause' — it allows the Centre to take over state administration when a state's constitutional machinery fails.
subject: Polity

stem: The Sarkaria Commission (1988) recommended that President's Rule should be used:

options.option_text: More frequently to maintain Centre-State balance
Freely by the Centre whenever elections are due
As a last resort, only after exhausting all alternatives to restore constitutional government
Only on recommendation of the Supreme Court

explanation: The Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State Relations recommended that Article 356 should be used sparingly, as a last resort, and only when there is objective material to conclude that State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.
subject: Polity

stem: A resolution to revoke a National Emergency can be passed by the Lok Sabha with:

options.option_text: A simple majority of total Lok Sabha membership
An absolute majority (50%+1 of all members)

explanation: The 44th Amendment allows Lok Sabha to revoke National Emergency by passing a resolution by a simple majority of the total membership of the Lok Sabha (even if Parliament is NOT in session — a special sitting can be convened).
subject: Polity

stem: Article 355 places a duty on the Union to protect every State against:
explanation: Article 355 — Duty of the Union to protect states against external aggression and internal disturbance and to ensure that the government of every State is carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.
subject: Polity

stem: During President's Rule (Article 356), the functions of the State legislature are exercised by:

options.option_text: The State Cabinet in caretaker capacity

explanation: When President's Rule is imposed, the State Legislature is either suspended or dissolved. Parliament assumes the legislative powers of the State Legislature and can make laws on subjects in the State List.
subject: Polity

stem: The most prolonged President's Rule in any Indian state was in which state?
explanation: Jammu & Kashmir had the most prolonged President's Rule periods — including a continuous stretch from 2018–2019. It was also governed as a Union Territory for a period after the abrogation of Article 370 in 2019.
subject: Polity

stem: Financial Emergency (Article 360) requires the approval of both Houses of Parliament within:
explanation: Financial Emergency must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within 2 months from the date of its proclamation. If Parliament is dissolved, it must be approved within 30 days of the Lok Sabha's reconstitution.
subject: Polity

stem: During which Emergency was the 42nd Constitutional Amendment — the most extensive amendment — passed?
explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) — nicknamed the 'mini-Constitution' — was passed during the 1975 Internal Emergency under Indira Gandhi. It added Fundamental Duties, changed the Preamble (added 'socialist' and 'secular'), and curtailed judicial review powers.
subject: Polity

stem: Article 352 proclamation must be approved by Parliament by a special majority. Special majority here means:

options.option_text: 2/3 majority of members present and voting, which must not be less than 1/2 of total membership

explanation: Article 368 / Article 352 special majority = 2/3 of members present and voting in each House AND this majority must constitute at least half the total membership. Both conditions must be satisfied simultaneously.
subject: Polity
